frequency_question: How often do legislative majorities with explicit intent pass major restrictive voting eligibility bills within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major bills pushed by legislative majorities requiring new documentation for voting/registration; excludes non-voting procedural resolutions and consensus technical corrections.

cases.name: Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (partial analogue for major electoral rules)
For the People Act (H.R. 1 / S. 1) - House passage
Freedom to Vote Act - Senate cloture attempts
Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act - House passage

provenance_note: claimed 3 hits but 4 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 major instances enumerated representing high-priority electoral bills under unified or polarized legislative control.
known_gaps: Excludes minor state-level precursors or rider amendments not receiving standalone votes.
skeleton: Legislative majorities prioritizing electoral rules during polarized sessions: 5 major attempts identified, resulting in 3 single-chamber or full legislative passages of major electoral integrity/reform bills.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 comparable major party-backed electoral integrity push cycles.
validity_reason: Holds as long as current congressional polarization and party polarization on election administration persist through the next congressional cycle.
